title: Telemetry commit frames for idempotent billing
creator: Devon Park
description: Proposal: implement a "commit frame" protocol for telemetry/usage ingest so that L7 clients can pre-commit usage bundles (frames) and later finalize or abort them. Each frame contains a deterministic frame-id derived from customer, route, and granular sequence-slot. Servers persist provisional credits on frame precommit and move them to finalized accounting upon commit. This enables at-least-once networks and client retries without double-charging while keeping latency low for fast-path accept/ack. The protocol has three operations: FRAME_PRECOMMIT, FRAME_COMMIT, FRAME_ABORT. We will store frames in a compact per-customer ledger with soft-expiry tombstones and a reconciliation sweep for frames older than X. Design goals: zero-duplicate-billing under common retry patterns, bounded storage per-customer, quick failure-path to avoid charge orphans, compatibility with Dedicated/Dedicated-Edge and Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Client can precommit frames with idempotent response code and provisional reserve recorded
Commit moves provisional reserve to finalized usage ledger and emits billing event exactly once
Abort cancels provisional reserve and frees capacity
Telemetry retention and reconciliation sweep clears expired provisional frames without double-billing
Integration tests simulate at-least-once retries and network partitions proving no duplicate charges
design_decisions: Use deterministic frame-id combining customer_id + route_hash + 64-bit monotonic slot seeded per session to avoid cross-client collisions
Persist provisional state in per-tenant bounded ledger (rocksdb) rather than global DB to limit blast radius
Soft-expiry TTL default 7 days with reconciliation job incremental by customer to reduce tail latency on deletes
Avoid global locks; use CAS-based finalization with event-sourcing style append-only commit log to enable replay and audit
tradeoffs: Provisional reserves increase short-term memory footprint and require reconciliation; we accept bounded storage for correctness
Using per-tenant ledgers complicates cross-tenant reporting for aggregated dashboards; will emit summarized events to metrics pipeline
Deterministic IDs shift collision risk to incorrect client implementations; mitigated with validation heuristics and server-side session stamping
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Proto API + wire-format + SDK helpers (2 weeks)
Phase 2: Server-side per-tenant ledger and precommit/commit/abort handlers (3 weeks)
Phase 3: Integration tests, chaos tests (network partition, duplicate sends) and bench (1 week)
Phase 4: Canary rollout on staging then production with telemetry gating (2 weeks)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: orphan provisional frames leading to accidental long-term reserved credits -> Mitigation: auto-abort policy + reconciliation sweep with owner alerts
Risk: increased write amplification -> Mitigation: compacted append-only log and periodic compaction
Risk: client library adoption delay -> Mitigation: server accepts legacy flow and emits warning telemetry
